title: 6th International Conference on Concussion in Sport - Amsterdam 2022 Consensus Statement
claims: Relative rest with activities of daily living is preferred to strict rest during the first 24-48 hours.
Light physical activity such as walking can begin within 24-48 hours when tolerated and without meaningful symptom worsening.
Reduced screen use is most relevant during the first 48 hours.
Persistent dizziness, balance problems, neck pain, or headaches may warrant cervicovestibular rehabilitation and clinical reassessment.
Return-to-learn and return-to-sport decisions should be gradual, individualized, and symptom-guided.

title: Managing Return to Activities
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention HEADS UP
claims: Return to daily activities, school, work, and sport should be individualized and guided by symptoms and cognitive function.
Symptoms that return or worsen during exertion should guide a reduction in activity and clinical follow-up.
Return-to-play progression requires monitoring after each step and should pause when new symptoms appear.
Referral should be considered when symptoms worsen, persist beyond 2-4 weeks, or risk factors for prolonged recovery are present.

title: What to do After a Concussion
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention HEADS UP
claims: A person with a possible concussion should be evaluated by a healthcare provider.
Light physical activity such as walking may be appropriate early in recovery, while sports and re-injury risk should be avoided until cleared.
Students may return to school within 1-2 days with accommodations that are gradually reduced as function improves.
Symptoms lasting longer than 2-4 weeks or worsening symptoms warrant healthcare-provider follow-up and possible specialist referral.

title: Guidelines for Recovery
claims: Recovery guidance should discourage prolonged isolation or cocooning and support relative rest.
Activity should be reduced when symptoms increase more than mildly or remain elevated after exercise.
Social connection and mental well-being are relevant parts of concussion recovery.
